script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 11. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You don't decide to brush your teeth each morning—you just do it.  Habits are behaviors so repeated they've become automatic.  Nearly half your daily actions run on autopilot.

Habits remove decision from repetition. This is powerful for good or bad. Good habits build you automatically. Bad habits destroy you automatically. The autopilot flies toward whatever you've programmed. Habits follow a loop: cue triggers routine which delivers reward.  Understanding this loop lets you design new habits and disrupt old ones.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You become what you repeatedly do.  Habits are the compound interest of behavior.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Habit Audit - What's Running on Autopilot?.

Here's your activity: List your daily habits—morning routine, eating patterns, work behaviors, evening activities. Which serve your goals? Which undermine them? Pick one to build or break this month. This helps you identify automatic behaviors and evaluate their effects.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about things you do without thinking can be applied to habit audit - what's running on autopilot?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
